answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and buys one timber futures contract, bound to its key. The contract promises timber fuel at the 40-credit rate, and settles at the horizon: the forge must show receipts matching it, auditor-checked before the horizon closes. A futures-rental ring fails: a rented contract settles to the owner key, so the renter forge shows no receipts and the bond burns. The kth fake needs its timber contract and bond, so 1,000 fakes pay 40,000 for timber futures plus 70,000 at risk, with no pooling discount. An honest identity buys one contract and keeps its bond.
